subject: zerogxplode
leg: control: Valve's own against the brief
label: sprites/zerogxplode.spr, in the place of the game's own

R1.reason: Reads as an explosion throughout: a small hot spark at frame 0, a white-hot fireball bursting at frames 1 to 4, lobes forming and billowing at frames 5 to 7, then yellow-orange lobes at frames 8 to 11 that sink and dim to nothing by frame 14. Debris specks fly off the edges. This matches the brief's 'bursts, billows into lobes, burns away to nothing'.

R2.reason: Each 64x64 frame holds the effect in its centre without touching the cell edges (e.g. the frame 2 and 3 blobs span roughly half the cell width). The effect grows and then shrinks to a small ember, as the original's would. The measured border max of 0.818 is most likely the white frame-number labels sitting on each cell's top-left border, not the sprite, since no frame shows light running to an edge; the border mean of 0.005 is within the class.

R3.reason: By eye the colour sequence is right for an additive fireball: white-hot core in frames 1 to 4, pale yellow in 5 to 7, golden orange with darker red-brown lobes in 8 to 11, and dull dark red in 12 to 14. Against the black background it blends as additive light should.

R4.reason: Fifteen frames, the same count as the class. The envelope sits inside the explosion class: the peak at 0.36 of the run (frame 5), first frame 0.08 and last 0.03, both within their ranges. It grows, then burns away, and the one-shot ends dark (frame 14 is a faint ember, last frame dark). Jitter of 1.25 is inside the class range of 1.04 to 1.48, so the motion is steady rather than flickering.

R5.reason: Its type (parallel) and format (additive) match the game's file as measured, under the same name, and it reads back as written. Frames are on a black background, so additive blending adds nothing beyond the effect.
